questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Who broke the glass?
options: By whom was the glass broken?
By whom is the glass broken?
By whom has the glass been broken?
Who was the glass broken by whom?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Who + V2 + O' becomes 'By whom + was + O + V3'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: He said to me, “What is your name?”
options: He asked me what is my name.
He asked me what my name was.
He asked me what was my name.
He asked me what his name was.
questions.explanation: Rule: wh-question gets statement order; is becomes was; 'your' becomes 'my'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Does he play chess?
options: Was chess played by him?
Are chess played by him?
Is chess played by him?
Does chess played by him?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Does + S + V1 + O' becomes 'Is/Are + O + V3 + by S'; 'chess' is singular so 'Is'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Did she help you?
options: Are you helped by her?
Was you helped by her?
Have you been helped by her?
Were you helped by her?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Did + S + V1 + O' becomes 'Was/Were + O + V3 + by S'; 'you' takes 'were'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: The teacher said to Ravi, “Are you ill?”
options: The teacher asked Ravi if he was ill.
The teacher asked Ravi if you were ill.
The teacher asked Ravi if he is ill.
The teacher asked Ravi that he was ill.
questions.explanation: Rule: yes/no question uses 'if'; are becomes was; 'you' becomes 'he'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Is Ravi writing a letter?
options: Was a letter being written by Ravi?
Is a letter being written by Ravi?
Is a letter written by Ravi?
Has a letter been written by Ravi?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Is + S + V-ing + O' becomes 'Is + O + being + V3 + by S'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Will you help the poor?
options: Would the poor be helped by you?
Will the poor helped by you?
Will the poor be helped by you?
Will the poor have been helped by you?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Will + S + V1 + O' becomes 'Will + O + be + V3 + by S'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: He said to her, “Where did you go?”
options: He asked her where did she go.
He asked her where she went.
He asked her where he had gone.
He asked her where she had gone.
questions.explanation: Rule: wh-question uses statement order; simple past becomes past perfect; 'you' becomes 'she'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Have they finished the work?
options: Has the work been finished by them?
Have the work been finished by them?
Had the work been finished by them?
Was the work finished by them?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Have + S + V3 + O' becomes 'Has/Have + O + been + V3 + by S'; 'work' is singular so 'Has'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: She said to me, “Do you know him?”
options: She asked me if she knew him.
She asked me if I knew him.
She asked me do I know him.
She asked me if I know him.
questions.explanation: Rule: yes/no question uses 'if'; present becomes past; 'you' becomes 'I'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Can you solve this sum?
options: Could this sum be solved by you?
Can this sum solved by you?
Can this sum be solved by you?
Is this sum solved by you?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Modal + S + V1 + O' becomes 'Modal + O + be + V3 + by S', keeping 'can'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: “Why are you laughing?” Rani said to Mohan.
options: Rani asked Mohan why was he laughing.
Rani asked Mohan why you were laughing.
Rani asked Mohan why he had laughed.
Rani asked Mohan why he was laughing.
questions.explanation: Rule: wh-question uses statement order; present continuous becomes past continuous; 'you' becomes 'he'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Why do they sell tickets so early?
options: Why are tickets sold so early?
Why were tickets sold so early?
Why are tickets selling so early?
Why do tickets sold so early?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Why do + S + V1 + O' becomes 'Why are + O + V3'; the vague agent 'they' is dropped.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: What did the teacher give you?
options: What are you given by the teacher?
What were you given by the teacher?
What was you given by the teacher?
What had you been given by the teacher?
questions.explanation: Rule: with two objects, 'you' becomes the subject; 'did give' becomes 'were given'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Whom did you invite?
options: Who is invited by you?
Whom was invited by you?
Who was invited by you?
Who were invited by you?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Whom + did + S + V1' becomes 'Who + was + V3 + by S' because the questioned word is now the subject.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Whose pen did he take?
options: Whose pen is taken by him?
Whose pen did he taken?
Whose pen has been taken by him?
Whose pen was taken by him?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Whose + noun' acts as the object phrase and becomes the subject: 'was taken by him'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: He said to me, “How are you?”
options: He asked me how I was.
He asked me how was I.
He asked me how he was.
He asked me how am I.
questions.explanation: Rule: wh-question uses statement order; are becomes was; 'you' becomes 'I'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Mother said to Seetha, “Why have you not eaten?”
options: Mother asked Seetha why she has not eaten.
Mother asked Seetha why she had not eaten.
Mother asked Seetha why had she not eaten.
Mother asked Seetha why you had not eaten.
questions.explanation: Rule: present perfect becomes past perfect; statement order; 'you' becomes 'she'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: The manager said to him, “Where will you stay in Chennai?”
options: The manager asked him where he will stay in Chennai.
The manager asked him where would he stay in Chennai.
The manager asked him where he would stay in Chennai.
The manager asked him where you would stay in Chennai.
questions.explanation: Rule: will becomes would; statement order; 'you' becomes 'he'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: How did he solve the puzzle?
options: How is the puzzle solved by him?
How did the puzzle solved by him?
How has the puzzle been solved by him?
How was the puzzle solved by him?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'did + V1' becomes 'was + V3'; the question word stays first.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: “Shall we go for a walk?” said Vimal to Karthik.
options: Vimal suggested to Karthik that they should go for a walk.
Vimal asked Karthik if they shall go for a walk.
Vimal suggested to Karthik that we should go for a walk.
Vimal asked Karthik whether he went for a walk.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'Shall we' (a suggestion) becomes 'suggested that ... should'; 'we' becomes 'they'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Do it at once.
options: It is done at once.
Let it be done at once.
Let it done at once.
Let it was done at once.
questions.explanation: Rule: an imperative becomes 'Let + O + be + V3'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: The coach said to the players, “Don't lose heart.”
options: The coach advised the players that they not lose heart.
The coach asked the players if they lost heart.
The coach advised the players not to lose heart.
The coach advised the players to not lost heart.
questions.explanation: Rule: a negative imperative becomes 'advised/told ... not to + V1'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Who has opened the box?
options: By whom was the box opened?
By whom had the box been opened?
By whom has the box opened?
By whom has the box been opened?
questions.explanation: Rule: present perfect passive is 'has + been + V3'; 'Who' becomes 'By whom'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Where did they keep the keys?
options: Where were the keys kept?
Where are the keys kept?
Where was the keys kept?
Where have the keys been kept?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'did + V1' becomes 'were + V3' for the plural 'keys'; the vague agent 'they' is dropped.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Who teaches you science?
options: By whom were you taught science?
By whom are you taught science?
By whom are you being taught science?
By whom is science taught you?
questions.explanation: Rule: simple present gives 'are + V3' (no 'being'); 'Who' becomes 'By whom'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: He asked me whether I would join the club.
options: He said to me, “Would you join the club?”
He said to me, “Will he join the club?”
He said to me, “Will you join the club?”
He said to me, “Do you join the club?”
questions.explanation: Rule: 'whether' clause becomes an inverted direct question; would becomes will; 'I' becomes 'you'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: By whom was the letter posted?
options: Who posts the letter?
Whom posted the letter?
Who has posted the letter?
Who posted the letter?
questions.explanation: Rule: 'By whom + was + O + V3' becomes 'Who + V2 + O'.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: People say that honesty pays.
options: It is said that honesty pays.
It was said that honesty pays.
It is said that honesty paid.
Honesty is said that pays.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'People say that ...' becomes 'It is said that ...'; the present tense is retained.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Everyone expected that he would win.
options: It is expected that he would win.
It was expected that he would win.
It was expected that he will win.
He was expected that would win.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'S + V2 + that-clause' becomes 'It was + V3 + that-clause'; the that-clause is unchanged.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: He said to her, “Please do not leave me.”
options: He requested her not to leave me.
He ordered her do not leave him.
He requested her not to leave him.
He requested her that she did not leave him.
questions.explanation: Rule: a polite negative command becomes 'requested ... not to + V1'; 'me' becomes 'him'.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: She said, “How I wish I were a bird!”
options: She wished that I were a bird.
She wished that she is a bird.
She asked how she wished to be a bird.
She wished that she were a bird.
questions.explanation: Rule: an exclamation of wish becomes 'wished that'; 'I' becomes 'she'; the subjunctive 'were' is retained.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: Someone must have left the gate open.
options: The gate must have been left open.
The gate must be left open.
The gate must have left open.
The gate had been left open.
questions.explanation: Rule: 'modal + have + V3' becomes 'modal + have been + V3'; the indefinite agent 'someone' is dropped.
questions.shortcut: First spot the tense and sentence type, then apply its rule: questions need statement order in reported speech, inverted order in direct speech.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct transformation of: The doctor said to the patient, “If you take rest, you will recover soon.”
options: The doctor told the patient that if he takes rest, he will recover soon.
The doctor told the patient that if he took rest, he would recover soon.
The doctor told the patient that if I took rest, I would recover soon.
The doctor told the patient that if he took rest, he had recovered soon.
questions.explanation: Rule: in a conditional, the present tense becomes past and will becomes would; 'you' becomes 'he'.
